title: When the Colony Wakes Anew
premise: Casper Okafor investigates the impossible: a colony ship, Meridian, returns from a forty-year deep-space run with its crew aged backward, memories intact but bodies decades younger, and no record of what happened in the dark between stars. As Casper digs through falsified manifests and a war both homeworlds pretend is over, they uncover that Meridian's crew found the enemy's origin world — and chose to erase the evidence to buy peace. The message Casper must deliver is the truth of that choice, and delivering it means exposing their own hidden identity as a child of the erased colony. In the end, Casper broadcasts the message as the jump window closes, forcing both worlds to face a shared crime; the war does not end cleanly, but it ends, and Casper finally stops running.
about_author: Mirabel Villalobos is a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years adjudicating claims for vessels lost in contested waters before turning to fiction. She writes from a houseboat off the coast of Veracruz, where she keeps a logbook of every ship that never came home.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Casper Okafor. Casper works the shipping lanes between two worlds that severed contact years ago, investigating 'impossible accidents' that are really cover-ups. A routine claim on a derelict freighter reveals coordinates pointing toward the forbidden Meridian corridor. The beat is weary competence masking loneliness; Casper's invisibility feels like safety until this chapter cracks it.

chapters.title: Everyone Aged Backward
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The colony ship Meridian docks unannounced, its entire crew biologically twenty years younger than their service records, memories intact. Casper is assigned the investigation because no one else will touch it. Interviews reveal gaps: forty days missing from every log, all synchronized. Emotional beat: uncanny dread braided with fascination — Casper recognizes one crew member and says nothing.

chapters.title: What the Manifests Hide
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Reyes, Meridian's captain, now physically thirty but carrying sixty years of memory. Flashbacks show the crew discovering an inhabited world in the corridor — the enemy's cradle — and a vote taken in the dark. Ilsa burned the evidence herself. Beat: guilt worn as command authority; she watches Casper investigate and lets him, testing whether he can be trusted with the truth.

chapters.title: The Child of the Erased Colony
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Cross-referencing Meridian's passenger list against his own forged identity papers, Casper confirms he was born on the world the crew voted to erase from the record — not destroyed, but deleted, its existence scrubbed to end the war. His parents' names appear on the manifest. Beat: identity collapse; the investigator realizes he has been investigating himself all along.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Silence
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Both governments move to seize Meridian; Ilsa plays them against each other while secretly preparing a broadcast of the full voyage record. Her second-in-command, Voss, argues the deletion was mercy and must stay buried. Beat: power's seduction — Ilsa feels how easy it would be to simply become the arbiter of truth rather than its messenger.

chapters.title: Voss's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Voss, the crew's ethicist turned saboteur. He sabotages the broadcast array and frames Casper for espionage, believing renewed contact between the worlds would reignite the war and kill millions. His logic is airtight and monstrous. Beat: chilling sympathy — Voss genuinely grieves even as he destroys, embodying survival purchased with other people's erasure.

chapters.title: Forty Days in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Casper, imprisoned pending charges. Ilsa smuggles him the recovered black-box fragment: the forty missing days show the crew did not destroy the corridor world — they hid it, and the aging reversal was the price of the jump back, paid by everyone aboard. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve; Casper understands the message isn't accusation but confession, and confessions need a witness.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The window through which Meridian arrived — and through which proof could reach the neutral relay — closes in seventy-two hours. Ilsa mutinies against her own government's boarding party, spending her remaining authority and her crew's loyalty in one irreversible act. Beat: the cost made flesh; she trades her career, her freedom, and possibly her life for a message she may never see delivered.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Climax. Casper fights through Voss's sabotage to the transmitter, choosing to append his own testimony — his name, his birthworld, his parents — to Meridian's record, making the message personal and undeniable. Voss stands down at the last moment, unable to watch another person pay the price he demanded of everyone else. The transmission goes out as the window seals. Beat: terror, then stillness.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: POV Casper, months later. The broadcast forces both worlds into open reckoning; the war formally ends not with treaties but with shared acknowledgment of the corridor world, now reopened to contact. Casper, publicly named, chooses to stay visible — taking work as an advocate for the disappeared rather than an investigator of accidents. Final beat: quiet hope; survival's price was paid, and someone finally kept the receipt.
